docs.title: Materials: cards, parameters and what a card does
docs.text: A softsim material is a card: one YAML file (or mapping) that holds everything about a soft material that a simulation needs, plus where the numbers come from and how far they can be trusted. Every number on a card can be changed the same way as any other config value.

docs.title: A card
docs.text:
name: my_silicone
description: What it is.
source: Where every number comes from. Say "uncalibrated" or "fitted to X" honestly.
kind: physical                # physical | effective (see below)
density: 1070 kg/m^3
elastic:
  model: yeoh                 # linear | stvk | neo_hookean | stable_neo_hookean | mooney_rivlin | yeoh
  c10: 12 kPa                 #   | ogden | gent | arruda_boyce | magneto_active
  c20: 0.8 kPa
  poisson_ratio: 0.49         # or bulk_modulus: 1.2 MPa
damping:                      # optional
  model: prony                # prony (a material model) | rayleigh | kelvin_voigt (numerical damping)
  g: [0.5, 0.2]
  tau: [2 ms, 50 ms]
friction: {sliding: 1.0}
adhesion: {strength: 14 kPa, range: 0.3 mm}   # optional tack (cohesive law)
validity:                     # where the data behind the card was taken
  strain: [-0.5, 3.0]         # nominal uniaxial strain range
  strain_rate: [0 1/s, 300 1/s]
  temperature: 23 degC
uncertainty:                  # one standard deviation (normal, lognormal) or half-width (uniform)
  elastic.c10: {rel: 0.08}
  damping.g[0]: {abs: 0.05, dist: uniform}
references:
  - {doi: 10.1089/soro.2019.0115, note: uniaxial tension data}

Elastic laws. All laws accept unit strings ("12 kPa"). Their parameters:

model parameters notes linear, stvk, neo_hookean, stable_neo_hookean any two of youngs_modulus, poisson_ratio, shear_modulus, bulk_modulus stored as E and ν mooney_rivlin c10, c01 yeoh c10, c20, c30 often the best simple fit for silicones ogden mu: [...], alpha: [...] N terms gent mu, jm stiffens without bound as I1 − 3 → J_m arruda_boyce mu, lambda_m five-term series (Abaqus form); locking stretch λ_m magneto_active matrix (any hyperelastic law above), susceptibility or particle_volume_fraction, along, normal, demagnetization iron-filled (MRE): soft-magnetic in the scene's magnetic_field; reference backend only (magnetic.md)

The laws with a bulk modulus take bulk_modulus or poisson_ratio. softsim material show <card> prints the small-strain equivalents (E0, μ0, κ, ν0), wave speeds and explicit time-step estimates of any card.

Rate dependence. prony is a material model: generalised Maxwell relaxation of the shear (isochoric) part, G(t) = G0 (1 − Σ g_i (1 − e^(−t/τ_i))). The elastic constants are the instantaneous ones, so the long-term shear modulus is G0 (1 − Σ g). rayleigh and kelvin_voigt are numerical damping: their loss grows without bound with frequency. They help stabilise or match one experiment, but they are not a description of a silicone.

Prony runs on every solver with the same update and energies:

  • the reference FEM and the homogeneous tests;
  • MuJoCo and SOFA. There the backend's own elasticity carries the long-term law, and the decaying Maxwell overstresses are added as vertex forces each step (softsim/materials/viscoelastic.py). These forces are explicit, so softsim check verifies that the time step resolves them.

Prony needs a law with an isochoric/volumetric split, so not linear or stvk.

Physical and effective cards. kind: physical means that the numbers describe the material and should hold on any solver that represents the law well. kind: effective means the numbers reproduce data only with one backend, mesh and contact model. Calibrating a backend against an experiment produces such cards (the *_drop_fit* presets). An effective card must name backend and mesh_size in its provenance.

docs.title: The library
docs.text:
softsim materials lists every card.

  • Preferred physical cards: the *_roels2025 cards for 7 silicones (Ecoflex 00-20/00-30/00-50, Dragon Skin 20/30, Mold Max 14NV, Mold Star 30). They are fitted to tension and compression specimens together (Roels et al. 2025, CC-BY-4.0), with a measured slow Prony series (1 s to 3 h). Ecoflex 00-30 and 00-50 also carry measured fast relaxation for impacts (see below).
  • Older physical cards: the *_marechal2021 cards for 18 silicones (Marechal et al. 2021), from tension only. Their moduli are probably ~3× too low, because the strain was measured at the crosshead.
  • All are listed with their fit quality and caveats in material_library.md.
  • Datasheet estimates: ecoflex_00_10, ecoflex_00_30, dragon_skin_10.
  • Effective drop-test fits: ecoflex_00_10_drop_fit*.

To fit your own data, write a kind: material_tests dataset file and run the commands below. See datasets/roels2025_elastomers.yaml for several test kinds and specimens per material, or datasets/marechal2021_srmd.yaml for one curve.

softsim fetch datasets/marechal2021_srmd.yaml                     # downloads + checks the archive
softsim fit-material datasets/marechal2021_srmd.yaml ecoflex_00_30 --strain-max 1.0
# every law: cards with uncertainty, report.yaml, fit.png in runs/material_fits/...
softsim material project ecoflex_00_30_marechal2021 --to neo_hookean --strain-range=-0.3,0.6 --out eco30_nh.yaml

fit-material fits neo_hookean, mooney_rivlin, yeoh, ogden1, ogden2, gent and arruda_boyce. It ranks them by AIC, reports parameter uncertainties, and flags laws that lose stability (stress decreasing with stretch) in uniaxial, equibiaxial or planar loading within the fitted range.

project fits another law to a card's own response, for backends that lack the card's law. MuJoCo has only stable Neo-Hookean, and its refusal message points to this command.

docs.title: Fast rate dependence (impacts)
docs.text:
Tension tests run at about 0.4/s, while an impact loads the material within milliseconds. Silicones are much stiffer and lossier there. Ecoflex 00-30, for example, is 1.65× stiffer at 100 Hz and 2.2× at 1 kHz than in its tension test. A card without fast-rate data is therefore too soft and too bouncy in impacts.

If you have a frequency-domain fit (DMA, rheometer, guided waves) as a fractional Kelvin–Voigt model μ0 (1 + (iωτ)ⁿ), convert it to Prony branches and add them to a card. The response at the test rate stays as fitted:

from softsim.materials import load_material, save_material
from softsim.materials.viscoelastic import prony_from_fractional, with_fast_relaxation

a, taus, rms = prony_from_fractional(n=0.20, tau=2.9e-3, band=(1.0, 2000.0))   # Hz
card = with_fast_relaxation(load_material("my_silicone"), a, taus)
save_material(card, "my_silicone_rate.yaml")
  • Band: branches are placed only inside the band. Keep its top below 1/(2π·dt) of the backend you run, and its bottom where your measured relaxation starts, so nothing is counted twice.
  • Source of the library's values: Croquette et al. 2026 (arXiv:2604.27722), who measured Ecoflex 00-30 and 00-50 with guided elastic waves and checked them against a rheometer from 1 to 100 Hz.
  • Assumption: only the shape of their curve relative to the test rate is used, applied to the isochoric part at large strain. Their samples were about 2× softer than Roels', so their static modulus is not used.

docs.title: Changing values
docs.text:
Every value is a dotted key, the same everywhere:

softsim params scenarios/drop_test/cases/w050.yaml --grep material   # every key, value, unit, allowed range
softsim run scenarios/drop_test/cases/w050.yaml \
    --set specimen.material.elastic.youngs_modulus='40 kPa' \
    --set specimen.material.damping.model=prony \
    --set 'specimen.material.damping.g=[0.6]' --set 'specimen.material.damping.tau=[2 ms]'
softsim material show ecoflex_00_10 --set elastic.model=gent --set elastic.mu='30 kPa' --set elastic.jm=20
  • Switching a law: setting elastic.model (or damping.model) keeps only the parameters the new law understands. Going from an E/ν law to one with a bulk modulus carries ν over.
  • List entries are indexed: elastic.mu[1], damping.tau[0].
  • Sweeps: the same keys work in sweep grids (softsim sweep).
  • Which values matter: softsim sensitivity runs a Morris screening over value ranges and reports each parameter's influence (μ*) and non-linearity/interaction (σ) on any summary metric: 
    softsim sensitivity scenarios/drop_test/cases/w050.yaml --metric peak_indentation --jobs 8 \
    --param "specimen.material.elastic.youngs_modulus=30 kPa:150 kPa" \
    --param "specimen.material.damping.beta=0.1 ms:3 ms" --param "drop.height=0.2:0.4"
  • Uncertainty propagation: softsim sweep sweep.yaml --sample 32 --seed 0 (or a sample: block in the sweep file) crosses the grid with 32 variants of the material, drawn from its card's uncertainty. The drawn values become sample.<key> columns of results.parquet.
  • Python: 
    from softsim.materials import load_material, sample
m = load_material("ecoflex_00_10", overrides=["elastic.youngs_modulus=40 kPa"])
m2 = m.with_overrides(["elastic.model=yeoh", "elastic.c10=12 kPa"])
variants = sample(card_with_uncertainty, 64, seed=0)  # draws from `uncertainty`
  • At run time:
  • Simulation.set_material(body, material, overrides) rebuilds the model;
  • set_material(body, None, overrides) changes the current material;
  • ROS: the set_material service takes the same overrides list.

docs.title: What a card does: homogeneous tests
docs.text:
softsim.materials.homogeneous computes the exact response of a card in the standard laboratory tests, without a mesh or a backend. It needs the fem extra (JAX). The energies and the Prony update are those of the reference FEM.

from softsim.materials.homogeneous import curve, relaxation, constant_rate, dma
curve(m, "uniaxial", [0.5, 1.5, 2.0])        # also equibiaxial, planar, simple_shear, volumetric, confined
curve(m, "uniaxial", [1.5], "instantaneous") # infinitely fast; default "relaxed" = equilibrium
relaxation(m, strain=0.05)                   # ramp-and-hold
constant_rate(m, "uniaxial", 2.0, rate=100)  # strain rate in 1/s
dma(m, [1, 10, 100])                         # storage and loss modulus vs frequency

softsim material plot ecoflex_00_10 my_silicone.yaml --tests uniaxial,simple_shear,relaxation,dma --out cards.png

These are checked against closed forms for every law (tests/test_homogeneous.py):

  • uniaxial, biaxial and planar stresses;
  • small-strain moduli;
  • Prony relaxation;
  • DMA against the analytic G*(ω).

docs.title: From a physical card to a backend (transfer)
docs.text:
A physical card holds on any solver that represents its law well. The tetrahedral backends don't fully do so: linear elements lock, and MuJoCo's contact loses energy. To find the parameters with which a backend reproduces a physical card in a given scenario:

  1. Run the card on the locking-free reference with the scenario's conditions, and save the runs as tracks. tools/make_reference_tracks.py does this for the drop test with each recording's measured impact (softsim.experiments.reference_tracks).
  2. Calibrate the backend against those tracks. This is an ordinary softsim calibrate (e.g. calibrations/transfer_ecoflex_00_10_mujoco.yaml). The result is the backend's effective card, and the remaining NRMSE is its error bar against the physical card.

For Ecoflex 00-10 in the drop test, the physical values are 143 kPa, 0.69 and 2 ms. With a 5 mm mesh:

  • MuJoCo reproduces the card within 3–10% using E0 = 66 kPa, g = 0.94, τ = 5.5 ms;
  • SOFA within 3–7% using 79.6 kPa, 0.77 and 2.7 ms (experiments.md).

A transferred card is only valid for loads like the ones it was transferred on. The MuJoCo card above (fitted on 20 and 50 g) relaxes 94% within a few milliseconds. Under 500 g it crushes the specimen until MuJoCo's tetrahedra invert, and the run stops with "simulation diverged".

docs.title: Joint fits: lab tests and dynamic data together
docs.text:
Lab tests fix the quasi-static stiffness. An impact sees the instantaneous one and how fast it relaxes. Neither alone pins down a viscoelastic card:

  • tension data can't tell how much of the stiffness relaxes within milliseconds;
  • the drop data can't tell what the material does a second later.

A calibration file can therefore include material-test terms next to its simulated cases (softsim.experiments.calibrate). They are evaluated on the card's homogeneous-test curves, take milliseconds, and add to the same cost:

cases: {w020: 1.0, w050: 1.0}
material_tests:
  # specimens from a dataset, one term per test kind and strain window
  - {dataset: ../datasets/roels2025_elastomers.yaml, material: ecoflex_00_30, kind: tension, strain: [0, 1.0]}
  # relaxation: the normalised hold, so it tests rate dependence only
  - {dataset: ../datasets/roels2025_elastomers.yaml, material: ecoflex_00_30, kind: relaxation}
  # or inline points: a datasheet's "100% modulus" is often all there is
  - {name: datasheet_100pct, points: {strain: [1.0], stress: [55 kPa]}, weight: 0.5}

A term's cost is its RMSE relative to the largest stress, averaged over specimens. The term is compared with the card's fully relaxed curve, unless it has a test rate: the dataset's strain_rate, or rate: in the entry. With a rate, a Prony card is loaded at that rate.

A relaxation term ramps the card to each recording's hold strain at rate (default 0.4/s) and holds it. Both curves are divided by their value at the start of the recorded hold, which begins hold_offset (default 1.3 s) after the ramp, as in Roels et al. 2025. Ecoflex 00-30's library card matches its 3-hour hold within 0.35%; without damping it is off by 1.4%.

Example: Ecoflex 00-10. The drop-only fit on the 3D reference (E0 ≈ 150 kPa, g ≈ 0.7) relaxes to E∞ ≈ 44 kPa. The datasheet's 100% modulus (55 kPa) implies about 94 kPa. Every point that drop-only fit has evaluated misses the datasheet by 40–60%. calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_fem_joint.yaml fits both together. After 80 evaluations: E0 = 190 kPa, g = 0.60, τ = 0.58 ms, E∞ = 76 kPa, the datasheet term 20% off (from 40–60%), the 20 g first contact 14% and the 50 g one 3% (experiments.md).

docs.title: Moving to a faster machine (GPU box)
docs.text: What to install, what to copy from the laptop, and which long jobs to run there. Git carries the code, datasets files and calibration files; it does not carry data/ or runs/ (both gitignored).

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone <repo> soft_package && cd soft_package
python3.10 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev,fem,fast,calib,mesh,video]"
# NVIDIA GPU: JAX with CUDA (same version range as the fem extra)
pip install -U "jax[cuda12]>=0.4.30,<0.7"
python -c "import jax; print(jax.devices())"        # should list a CUDA device
  • SOFA (optional): unpack the SOFA v26.06 binary and export SOFA_ROOT=.../SOFA_v26.06.00_Linux (backends/sofa.md).
  • ROS 2 Humble (optional): ros2.md.

docs.title: 2. Copy from the laptop
docs.text:
# from the laptop's repository root; NEW = user@gpu-box:path/to/soft_package
rsync -a data/processed/ NEW/data/processed/          # tracked drop recordings (372 KB)
rsync -a runs/calibration/ runs/reference_tracks/ NEW/runs/ --relative   # finished and running fits
  • Raw drop videos: the five *gram.zip files from Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23185808) go into data/raw/czopek2026/. They are only needed to re-track; the tracks in data/processed/ are enough for simulations and fits.
  • Material-test data: softsim fetch datasets/roels2025_elastomers.yaml and softsim fetch datasets/marechal2021_srmd.yaml. Both are downloaded and checked by checksum.

A calibration resumes from its runs/calibration/<name>/evaluations.jsonl: copied logs are replayed, not re-simulated.

docs.title: 3. Check
docs.text:
python -m pytest -q                       # the whole suite (slow checks included): 278 tests, 17 min on the RTX 3060 box
python -m pytest -q -m "not slow"         # without the slow checks (Ogden in 3D, the rotating mount's)
python tools/bench_fem.py                 # per-part timings of the 3D solver
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu python tools/bench_fem.py   # the same on the CPU, for comparison

On the laptop (8-core CPU, no GPU), a 5 mm 3D step takes about 1.1 s: about 45% element kernels and 30% PARDISO (reference_fem.md).

Measured on an RTX 3060 (12 GB, 8 cores, JAX 0.6.2): the GPU's float64 rate is only ~160 GFLOP/s (the CPU's 90; its float32 is 11 TFLOP/s), and PARDISO stays on the CPU, so the GPU helps only the element tangents. tools/bench_fem.py, per Newton iteration, GPU / CPU:

Mesh Tangents Tangents + assembly Solve 8 mm (1 215 dofs) 1.3 / 4.1 ms 4.8 / 5.6 ms 2.5 / 1.6 ms 5 mm (4 788 dofs) 5.4 / 17.4 ms 15.3 / 19.8 ms 12.8 / 12.7 ms 3 mm (24 609 dofs) 29.9 / 130.5 ms 76.7 / 183.5 ms 195 / 228 ms

A real calibration evaluation (20 g and 50 g, 5 mm, 11 ms) takes 58–69 s on the GPU and 73–83 s on the CPU, against ~8 min on the laptop. The two cases of --jobs 2 share the GPU. The bench's own drop line (about 3 s per 0.1 ms step) is slower than a real case because its short drop takes ~28 Newton iterations per step; ignore it.

  • Use the GPU anyway (a 15–20% gain), but expect the big win from the 8 cores and PARDISO, not CUDA.
  • Calibration logs replay: replaying a laptop evaluation here reproduces its numbers to 5e-8, so a run can continue across machines. Track files are part of the log's key (a digest), so a log fitted to other tracks is ignored.

docs.title: 4. Long jobs, in order
docs.text:
Job Command Laptop time What it answers Drop-only physical card on the 3D reference softsim calibrate calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_fem_prony.yaml --jobs 2 ~6 h (40 evaluations) E0, g, τ of Ecoflex 00-10 from 20 and 50 g, free of backend artefacts. Done on the laptop (147 kPa, 0.70, 2.24 ms; docs/experiments.md) Joint fit: drop + datasheet softsim calibrate calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_fem_joint.yaml --jobs 2 ~6 h (40 evaluations; ~50 min here, with other jobs running, plus ~25 min for the plots of all five weights) whether one card fits impacts and the quasi-static stiffness (materials.md). Done: 80 evaluations, 190 kPa / 0.60 / 0.58 ms (experiments.md) Reference tracks of the fitted card python tools/make_reference_tracks.py --calibration calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_fem_joint.yaml --force ~20 min the target for the backend transfers MuJoCo and SOFA transfers softsim calibrate calibrations/transfer_ecoflex_00_10_{mujoco,sofa}.yaml --jobs 2 5 min / 35 min each backend's effective card and its error bar All-weights validation python tools/validate_drop_bounces.py ~10 min the acceptance table in experiments.md

With --jobs 2 each case runs in its own process. More jobs don't help a two-case calibration. On a many-core machine, run two calibrations side by side instead.

docs.title: Reference FEM (locking-free, axisymmetric and 3D)
docs.text:
softsim.fem holds two small finite-element solvers that give mesh-converged answers for the general backends (MuJoCo flex, SOFA) to be checked against. Both of those use linear tetrahedra, which lock for nearly incompressible materials, so their fitted moduli are "effective" values tied to a mesh.

  • softsim.fem.axisym: axisymmetric (cylinders, centred punches, uniaxial tests). Fast.
  • softsim.fem.solid3d: 3D, any geometry, rigid bodies with 6 DOF. It is also available as the backend fem (softsim run ... --backend fem). It is slow, about 1 s per step on a 5 mm mesh on a laptop (see Performance), but exact where the others are not.
pip install -e ".[fem]"     # JAX (CPU, float64) for exact tangents
python -m pytest tests/test_fem_axisym.py

from softsim.fem.drop import run_drop, FemSettings
ts, info = run_drop("scenarios/drop_test/cases/w050.yaml", ["simulation.duration=0.012"],
                    FemSettings(cells_r=16, cells_z=10))

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Elements: 6-node quadratic triangles in the r–z half-section with one dilatation per element (mean dilatation, P2/P0). No volumetric locking, up to incompressibility.
  • Materials: isochoric/volumetric split, JAX-traceable laws: Neo-Hookean (also used for stable_neo_hookean), Mooney-Rivlin, Yeoh, Ogden. Prony viscoelasticity acts on the isochoric part (Abaqus convention). Volumetric energy κ/4 (J² − 1 − 2 ln J).
  • Solver: each step minimises an incremental potential (elastic + Prony history + inertia + gravity + contact). Newton uses exact JAX tangents, an energy line search, a projected-Hessian fallback where the tangent is indefinite, and automatic step halving. The energy is infinite for any folded quadrature point (r–z fold or crossing the axis), so inverted states are never accepted.
  • Dynamics: Newmark with γ = ½ + a, β = (1 + a)²/4. The drop uses a = 0.25: with penalty contact, smaller values gained energy when contact released. This costs about 5% of the energy per impact.
  • Contact: a rigid flat punch (one vertical degree of freedom, the falling weight) and the ground, by penalty on boundary nodes with their exact annular tributary areas. Tangentially it is frictionless, sticking, or Coulomb (an incremental friction potential with the lagged normal pressure, C¹ stick zone), with the same cohesive adhesion law as softsim.materials.Adhesion. Both the punch and the ground can touch the top, bottom and side surfaces: under full-face loads the side bulges and rolls down onto the table. An earlier version let it pass through, which made a 500 g drop far too soft. Contact is node-based because, with quadratic edges in axisymmetry, the node on the axis gets exactly zero load from a uniform pressure, and quadrature-point contact let the punch pierce it.

docs.title: 3D solver and the fem backend
docs.text:
The formulation is the axisymmetric one, in 3D:

  • Elements: 10-node quadratic tetrahedra, built from any linear tetrahedral mesh by adding edge midpoints. There is one dilatation per element (P2/P0), so no locking.
  • Integration: an 8-point rule for stiffness and 27 points for mass.
  • Tangents: assembled from the 3×3 material tangents at the quadrature points. For invariant laws (Neo-Hookean, Mooney–Rivlin, Yeoh, Gent, Arruda–Boyce) they are in closed form and JAX only differentiates the scalar ψ(Ī₁, Ī₂). Ogden uses JAX derivatives of the full 3×3 energy.
  • Rigid bodies:
  • free mounts have 6 DOF: the centre-of-mass displacement and one incremental rotation vector per step. The gyroscopic term is neglected, which is exact for bodies spinning about their axis of symmetry.
  • slider_z mounts are springs with dampers. Bodies can also be fixed or prescribed.
  • Shapes are unions of cylinders and boxes with rounded edges, as exact signed distances.
  • Contact: node-based penalty with lumped areas. It is frictionless, sticking or Coulomb, with cohesive adhesion.
  • Viscoelasticity: Prony runs inside the implicit solve. Besides dynamics there is a quasi-static viscoelastic mode for relaxation tests.
  • Linear solves: MKL PARDISO when pip install -e ".[fast]" is installed, about 35× faster than SuperLU.

The fem backend maps a scene onto this solver:

  • one soft body;
  • every hyperelastic law and Prony. Ogden runs through matrix functions (tr C̄^(α/2) = tr exp((α/2) log C̄)), which are smooth where principal stretches coincide. Its tangents cost about 2 ms per quadrature point, roughly 100× the invariant laws, so project Ogden cards to Yeoh or Gent for long dynamic runs;
  • free and spring-mounted rigid bodies, and the ground;
  • friction: coefficients combine by maximum. 0 is frictionless, ≥ 1 is sticking (identical to μ = 1 statically, see below, and much faster for Newton), and anything in between is Coulomb. Coulomb is smoothed (IPC's mollifier) below a slip speed contact.slip_speed (default 1e-5 m/s), so a contact held below its limit creeps at a fraction of it, whatever the step (0.005 mm/s at 0.71 of the limit, benchmarks/sticking_block.yaml). Before 2026-11-11 the smoothing was 1 um per step (slip_speed: null), whose creep grows as the step shrinks (0.23 mm/s at 2 ms; decisions.md, entry 6);
  • adhesion from the material and the ground;
  • magneto-active (MRE) material in the scene's magnetic field, with solid magnets as rigid cylinders. See magnetic.md.

Rayleigh and Kelvin–Voigt damping are refused: they are numerical damping, so give the card a Prony series or no damping.

Check (tests/test_fem_3d.py) Result Quadrature, shape functions, mesh volume and surface exact Closed-form tangents vs JAX hessian, every invariant law, with Prony history within 1e-9 30% frictionless compression, Yeoh, between ground and a prescribed plate force within 0.1%, lateral stretch within 1e-4 of the homogeneous solution Quasi-static Prony ramp-and-hold plate force within 0.2% of the homogeneous history Rigid free flight and spin exact Centred 50 g drop (E = 100 kPa, ν = 0.4995, sticking) vs the axisymmetric solver 5 mm mesh: 5.53 mm at 4.04 ms; axisymmetric (converged): 5.75 mm at 4.14 ms

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
python tools/bench_fem.py times one Newton iteration of the drop-test specimen part by part (element tangents, energy, assembly, linear solve) and a short 50 g drop. Run it on each machine to compare.

  • Tangents: closed form for invariant laws, about 2× faster than differentiating the 3×3 energy twice. jnp.linalg.det was replaced by cofactor formulas, because JAX differentiates it through an LU factorisation.
  • Assembly: the Hessian's sparsity pattern (free DOFs, upper triangle) is fixed when the solver is built, from every element, contact candidate and rigid block. Each iteration only scatters values into it.
  • Linear solve: PARDISO's symbolic analysis (reordering) runs once per solver; each iteration only refactorises.
  • Compilation: compiled kernels are kept in ~/.cache/softsim/jax, so repeated runs on one mesh compile faster (9 → 6 s). Set SOFTSIM_JAX_CACHE to another directory, or to 0 to turn it off.

Together these took a short 8 mm drop from 75 s to 43 s on the laptop, with results matching the earlier code to the Newton tolerance.

Profile of a 5 mm, 50 g drop on the laptop (8 cores, shared with two other runs). A step takes about 4 Newton iterations and about 1.1 s.

Part of a Newton iteration Time Element tangents and their contraction into 30×30 matrices (JAX, mostly one core) ~110 ms (~45%) PARDISO refactorisation (MKL, multi-threaded) ~75 ms (~30%) Scatter into the fixed pattern, line-search energies, contact, Python the rest Once per run: JIT compilation of the kernels ~10 s

Solid3DSolver(..., quadrature=4) uses a 4-point stiffness rule, the one in Abaqus C3D10, instead of 8 points. In the drop it moved the peak by 0.5%. The default stays 8.

On a GPU: pip install -U "jax[cuda12]" and run the benchmark again. The element kernels run on the GPU unchanged. The linear solve stays on the CPU (PARDISO). Expect the kernel share to shrink a lot and the solve to dominate. JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu forces the CPU for comparison.

docs.title: Verified (tests/test_fem_axisym.py)
docs.text:
Check Result Volume of revolution, tributary areas exact (to 1e-12) 30% frictionless compression, Neo-Hookean, κ/μ = 10³ and 10⁵ force within 0.03% / 3·10⁻⁶ of incompressible theory; radius from volume conservation 20% compression, Mooney-Rivlin, 3-term Yeoh, Ogden (α = 3) within 0.2% of each law's exact uniaxial stress Bonded disc, ν = 0.49999, 3 meshes converges (2.7% then 1.05% change); E_c/E = 1.73, close to Gent's 1 + 2S² = 1.69. No locking Ramp-and-hold relaxation, Prony g = 0.5, τ = 0.1 s within 3% of the hereditary integral (the residue is real ringing) Static punch with Coulomb friction μ = 0 equals frictionless exactly; indentation falls monotonically with μ; μ = 10 equals stick

Friction matters as much as the modulus. At 20 N (E = 100 kPa, ν = 0.49) the static indentation is 3.91 mm frictionless, 3.08 mm at μ = 0.3, 2.56 mm at μ = 1 and 2.56 mm sticking. For a tacky silicone (μ ≈ 1), sticking contact is an excellent approximation.

docs.title: Static punch: MuJoCo vs reference
docs.text:
27 mm flat punch on the 40 × 17 mm cylinder, E = 54.8 kPa, ν = 0.45, sticking contact, static loads (MuJoCo: heavily damped, settled):

Load Reference (P2/P0, 16 × 10) MuJoCo, 5 mm mesh MuJoCo, 3.5 mm mesh 0.5 N 0.150 mm ~0.065 mm 1 N 0.291 mm ~0.19 mm 2 N 0.567 mm ~0.445 mm 5 N 1.327 mm 1.156 mm 1.358 mm 10 N 2.504 mm 2.269 mm 2.629 mm

The small-load MuJoCo values are corrected for a ~0.01 mm contact-skin offset. The reference is linear at small loads (about 3.5 kN/m, which agrees with a flat punch on a finite elastic layer) and stiffens at large ones. At large loads the two solvers agree within 2–5% once MuJoCo's mesh is 3.5 mm. The 5 mm mesh is 10–13% stiffer (locking), and more at small loads, where MuJoCo's soft contact also enters. Static elasticity and contact geometry are cross-validated.

docs.title: Drop test: where the solvers differ
docs.text:
For the 50 g drop with the M3 material (E = 54.8 kPa, ν = 0.45, no damping), the reference peaks at 7.7 mm (mesh-converged: 7.94 → 7.69 mm from 12 × 8 to 24 × 16). MuJoCo peaks at 4.9 mm on a 5 mm mesh and about 5.5 mm converged (5 → 3.5 → 2.5 mm: 4.94, 5.33, 5.46). Since static elasticity agrees (above), the difference comes from the impact dynamics:

  • MuJoCo depends strongly on friction: 4.89, 5.72 and 6.80 mm at μ = 1, 0.3 and 0. The reference sticks perfectly, which should make it the stiffest.
  • MuJoCo's undamped impact loses energy. Frictionless and without material damping, the weight's and specimen's kinetic energy plus gravity after separation is 77% of the input. With the specimen's (unreported) vibrational strain energy, roughly 10–25% is lost in the contact mechanics. This is independent of the timestep (0.1 to 0.01 ms) and of the contact damping ratio. With friction it loses more: soft constraints let the bulging specimen slip. The reference loses about 5%, to its numerical damping.
  • The material laws differ at large strain. MuJoCo uses Stable Neo-Hookean and the reference uses split Neo-Hookean. They are equal at small strain (the static table above), but the drop reaches 30–45% compression under the punch.

So MuJoCo's drop-test fit (E = 55 kPa, β = 0.31 ms) is an effective description that includes MuJoCo's own friction and contact losses, not the silicone's modulus and damping. Next steps: Stable Neo-Hookean in the reference (an F-bar form of a non-split energy, for a like-for-like law comparison) and fitting the material on the reference (below).

docs.title: What modulus does the real silicone have?
docs.text:
Since MuJoCo's drop-test fit includes MuJoCo's own contact losses, the reference solver asks the material question directly. Setup:

  • Neo-Hookean, ν = 0.4995;
  • sticking contact, no damping;
  • the measured impact speed;
  • first-contact comparison as in M3.
E 50 g peak / time (exp 4.31 mm / 3.7 ms) 20 g peak / time (exp 3.74 mm / 3.3 ms) 60 kPa 6.34 mm / 4.9 ms 5.15 mm / 3.5 ms 100 kPa 4.88 mm / 3.6 ms (NRMSE 13%) 3.94 mm / 3.0 ms 150 kPa 3.87 mm / 2.9 ms 3.13 mm / 2.4 ms

(20 g lands 6 mm off centre and is run centred, so it is approximate.)

  • E ≈ 100–130 kPa matches the peaks. That is in line with the Ecoflex 00-10 datasheet: its 100% modulus of 55 kPa means μ ≈ 31 kPa for a Neo-Hookean solid, so E ≈ 94 kPa, plus some stiffening at impact rates. MuJoCo's 55 kPa is an effective value.
  • No purely elastic E matches both peak and time to peak. The stiffness that gives the right depth peaks too early, the signature of material damping. tools/fit_reference_drop.py fits E together with one Prony term.

E + one Prony term (τ = 2 ms), fitted jointly on 50 and 20 g (12 × 8 mesh, Nelder–Mead, 30 evaluations, runs/reference_fit/w050_w020/):

E (instantaneous) g 50 g NRMSE (peak) 20 g NRMSE (peak) Joint best 143 kPa 0.69 20% (4.81 mm @ 3.7 ms) 15% (3.62 mm @ 2.9 ms) Best for 50 g alone 141 kPa 0.50 7.5% 34% Best for 20 g alone 125 kPa 0.73 35% 4.8%
  • The joint fit gives an instantaneous modulus of about 145 kPa relaxing by ~70% within a few ms, so a long-time modulus of about 45 kPa. Read it as an effective impact description, not material constants: a single fixed τ cannot represent a broad relaxation spectrum.
  • Each case fits well on its own, but not together. The two cases want different (E, g), and the joint error (18% mean) is no better than the elastic E = 100 kPa on 50 g (13%). Either one Prony term at τ = 2 ms is too simple (a free τ or two terms is the next step), or the 20 g case is biased, since it runs centred although the real weight landed 6 mm off centre and spinning. A 3D reference or an off-centre axisymmetric approximation would separate the two.
  • Caveat: the comparison rule. As everywhere on the experiment side, "contact" is when the weight's centre of mass departs from free fall by 0.1 mm (the tracker's noise limit), and the indentation counts from there. If the force builds slowly after the first touch, that point comes after some travel, in the recordings and in every simulation alike. The comparison is consistent, but it depends on how fast the force builds, and that differs between solvers: MuJoCo's soft contacts load abruptly, the reference's smooth contact gradually. For 500 g on the reference the detection fires several millimetres after the first touch, so its first-contact metric is not comparable. 500 g is left out of the reference fit.

docs.title: M1: core + MuJoCo drop test (done)
docs.text: Config and units, materials and presets, soft/rigid geometry, tetrahedral meshing, backend-neutral scene, capability system, MuJoCo flex backend, SOFA stub (replaced by the real backend in M4), physics checks, drop-test scenario with all five dataset weights, runner, sweeps, CLI, tests (including an analytic uniaxial check, convergence and no-penetration checks), and docs.

docs.title: M2: ROS 2 layer, Humble (done; see ros2.md)
docs.text:
• ros2/softsim_interfaces (ament_cmake): SoftBodyState, ContactWrench(Stamped), ScenarioMetrics, and services Reset, SetMaterial (preset name or YAML), RunAction (action name + YAML kwargs; drop = mass/height/preset).
  • ros2/softsim_ros (ament_python): a generic softsim_node that loads any scenario through Simulation (scenario:=… config:=… overrides:=[…]) and publishes /clock (simulated time; the simulation is ~0.005× real time), TF and pose/twist for rigid bodies, PointCloud2 and Marker mesh for soft bodies, metrics, contact wrenches and ground reaction.
  • ros2/softsim_bringup: launch with viewer on/off, headless batch mode, RViz config.

docs.title: M3: tracking + calibration (done; see experiments.md)
docs.text:
• Dataset registry (datasets/*.yaml: DOI, files, checksums, frame rate, overlay layout) and a loader that reads TIFFs straight from the zips.
  • Tracking: green-key background, per-weight appearance (brass vs black), translucent cylinder, base flash masked. Outputs weight top-edge/knob trajectory, cylinder top and bulge width; px→mm from the 40 mm diameter; time from the frame index (2999.3 fps), checked against the overlay.
  • Calibration: joint fit of (E, beta[, contact timeconst, friction]) across all five weights with scipy; coarse-to-fine mesh; per-case RMSE; fitted preset saved with mesh and backend provenance. Plots: sim vs experiment overlays, peak compression vs mass, rebound, settling, lift-off.

docs.title: M4: SOFA backend (done; see backends/sofa.md)
docs.text:
• SOFA v26.06 backend through SofaPython3, found via $SOFA_ROOT: linear, StVK, classic and stable Neo-Hookean, Mooney-Rivlin, one-term Ogden, Rayleigh/Kelvin-Voigt damping, rigid bodies, frictional Lagrange contact, bonded bases. Material mappings checked against analytic uniaxial compression; SOFA tests skip without SOFA.
  • stable_neo_hookean split from neo_hookean: MuJoCo's flex model is the stable variant and now says so; MuJoCo refuses classic Neo-Hookean.
  • Calibration hardening: blow-up guard in the SOFA backend (it segfaults instead of producing NaN), crash-tolerant and resumable calibrations, ground-penetration metric.
  • Results (experiments.md): Ogden fits 20/50 g within 3–11% but no material law fits 500 g; it prefers less large-strain stiffening than Neo-Hookean. Compressibility (ν = 0.45) explains part of the 500 g gap; rate dependence and the table are the remaining suspects.

docs.title: Direction
docs.text: softsim aims to be the soft-robotics package where every model is validated against real data, independent of the physics engine. It grows in three stages: validated sim-to-real (M1–M7, with soft materials first in M5), then design and control of real soft robots (M7–M11), then GPU learning (M12). Every robot family is planned (pneumatic, cable, gripper, magnetic). Every feature ships with a capability flag, a refusal where unsupported, an analytic test and a published-data validation.

docs.title: Drop test after the first contact (done, between M4 and M5)
docs.text:
See experiments.md.

  • Recordings re-read: the specimen hops and drags the cloth up; it is not the table moving (M3 was wrong). The first 100 ms are now usable data.
  • Contact adhesion (material.adhesion, ground.adhesion): a cohesive law, backend-neutral (softsim/contact/adhesion.py), on MuJoCo and SOFA, with an explicit-stiffness check, verified against analytic equilibria on both backends.
  • Spring-mounted rigid bodies (mount: slider_z, MuJoCo) and the drop test's compliant support.
  • Calibration over any observable and window (weight-relative position, specimen lift), not only the first contact.
  • Fixes in the SOFA backend: light rigid bodies (CG → direct solve) and pinned bodies on the ground (NaN).
  • Reference FEM (softsim.fem, reference_fem.md): axisymmetric P2/P0, locking-free, JAX tangents, Prony viscoelasticity, punch and ground contact, verified against analytic solutions. Its 50 g drop disagrees with MuJoCo by 40% (open).

docs.title: M5: soft-material fidelity (in progress)
docs.text:
Goal: a physical material card that runs with the same physics on every backend, with stated error. Every value can be changed from YAML, CLI, Python or ROS. The cards rest on public material-test data. Acceptance test: all five drop weights. See materials.md.

Done:

  • Material cards:
  • kind: physical | effective, validity, uncertainty, references;
  • any two isotropic constants as input; poisson_ratio for the bulk-modulus laws;
  • new laws Gent and Arruda–Boyce;
  • new units (1/s, J/m², Pa·s, K/°C, deg/s).
  • Parameterisation:
  • softsim params lists every changeable value with its unit and range;
  • softsim material show;
  • load_material(overrides=...), Material.with_overrides, sample() from the uncertainty;
  • Simulation.set_material(body, None, overrides) and the same overrides on the ROS set_material service.
  • Homogeneous tests (softsim.materials.homogeneous): uniaxial, equibiaxial, planar, simple shear, volumetric and confined. Also relaxation, constant-rate loading and DMA with Prony. All checked against closed forms, plus softsim material plot.
  • Public data and fitting:
  • the Marechal et al. 2021 tension data (ODbL; fetched, not redistributed);
  • softsim fit-material over 7 laws, with AIC/BIC, uncertainties and a stability check;
  • softsim material project for backends that lack a law; the backends' refusal messages point to it;
  • a generated library of 18 physical cards (material_library.md).
  • Prony viscoelasticity on MuJoCo and SOFA: the long-term law is native, and the Maxwell overstress is applied as explicit vertex forces with the reference's update (exact against the homogeneous reference). It comes with an explicit-stability check.
  • Drop validation over all five weights (tools/validate_drop_bounces.py). 20 and 50 g are reproduced. 100 and 200 g are tilted edge impacts. 500 g is stiffer and lossier than any model.
  • In-plane tilt at contact from the weights' side edges (softsim.experiments.video.tilt; reliable for the dark weights). It is applied in every simulation of a recording, and it brings 500 g's specimen hop to within 10%.
  • 3D locking-free reference (softsim.fem.solid3d, 10-node tetrahedra, P2/P0, 6-DOF rigid bodies, sticking, Coulomb and adhesive contact, Prony inside the implicit solve, PARDISO) and the fem backend. It is checked against homogeneous solutions, and against the axisymmetric solver within 4% on a coarse mesh.
  • A physical Ecoflex 00-10 card (Neo-Hookean 143 kPa + Prony 0.69 at 2 ms) reproduces the 20 and 50 g first contacts on the 3D reference within 7% and 10%, with each recording's offset and spin.
  • Transfer: reference runs saved as tracks; MuJoCo calibrated against them (3–10% error bar), SOFA likewise (3–7%, calibrations/transfer_ecoflex_00_10_sofa.yaml).
  • Second dataset: Roels et al. 2025 (CC-BY-4.0), tension, compression and 3 h relaxation for 7 silicones. Their cards are fitted to tension and compression together, with Prony from the relaxation, and are now the preferred ones (25 cards in the library). fit-material handles several specimens and test kinds.
  • Ogden in 3D through matrix functions (slow; project to Yeoh or Gent for long runs).
  • Joint fits: calibration files take material_tests terms (datasets or inline datasheet points) next to simulated cases. Prepared: calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_fem_joint.yaml, the drop plus the datasheet's 100% modulus. The drop-only card relaxes to about half the datasheet's quasi-static stiffness.
  • Sensitivity and uncertainty: softsim sensitivity (Morris screening) and softsim sweep --sample N from a card's uncertainty.
  • Contact fidelity, measured against the reference with elastic cards (tools/contact_restitution.py):
  • MuJoCo's flex elasticity is damped like backward Euler (ζ ≈ ω·dt/2);
  • its contact settings don't change impact losses;
  • without friction it is within 3.5% at meshes of 3.5 mm or finer, while soft-constraint friction slip costs about twice as much as everything else; contact.cone / contact.impratio mitigate part of it (backends/mujoco.md);
  • SOFA loses less with sticking friction, but much more frictionless.
  • 500 g:
  • out-of-plane tilt ruled out (a 20° sweep closes 17% of a 2× gap);
  • (since withdrawn: the two weights do not load the specimen alike, docs/experiments.md) a model-free check shows no passive specimen can explain it: the recording needs 12× the 50 g force at the same indentation and rate.
  • 3D solver ~1.8× faster (fixed sparsity pattern, PARDISO analysis once, closed-form tangents); tools/bench_fem.py for the GPU machine.

Next:

  • Long 3D fits on the faster machine (new_machine.md): the drop-only and the joint physical card, then new reference tracks and transfers.
  • Whole bounce in 3D (tack + support) for 20 and 50 g.
  • SOFA contact fidelity: the "58% loss" frictionless was a friction mismatch (SOFA uses one coefficient for every pair); with every pair frictionless it loses 3.4% more than the reference and peaks 14% shallow (2026-11-11, backends/sofa.md). Both open artefacts are closed (2026-11-12): the rim flare went 2.83 mm through the ground because a vertex moved 0.6 mm per step against a 0.4 mm alarm distance (the backend's alarm distance now follows the per-step travel: 0.006 mm), and the "7% stiff frictionless plate" was friction (a coefficient of about 0.1 anywhere in the scene; at 0 the plate agrees with no contact to 0.6%).
  • Rate data below 1 s (DMA or impact tests) for silicones. Today's relaxation data start at 1 s, while impacts relax within milliseconds.
  • 500 g: with the material excluded, check the setup and the measurement (a second camera view, or the original authors' notes).

docs.title: M6: foundations for robots (in progress)
docs.text:
Done so far (actuation.md): - Named surface regions on every soft shape, resolved on the mesh; fixed regions pin vertices. - Hollow shapes: hollow_sphere and closed_tube (balloon actuator), gmsh. - Pressure actuators on all three backends: exact -p V follower load in the reference; explicit follower forces on MuJoCo and SOFA. Schedules in YAML, set_control from Python, ROS 2 command and state topics. - inflation scenario (pressure–volume curve and extent). - Check: the reference matches the exact finite-strain thick-sphere solution within 0.1% up to 62% hoop strain, and it finds the limit pressure. - Backend error bar: at the same card, MuJoCo and SOFA agree with each other but inflate 27% less than the reference at 3 mm (13% at 2 mm): linear-tet locking at ν = 0.45. - softsim transfer (M5.6): fits a fast backend's effective card against the reference and checks it on unseen load cases. For MuJoCo at 3 mm, E 30 → 23.7 kPa takes the inflation error from 20% to 0.5%, and it holds at 1.5 and 4.5 kPa (1.2%, 2.2%). SOFA needs the same correction (23.6 kPa). - Bending actuator (off-axis cavity, scenarios/inflation/bending.yaml) with tip and bend-angle outputs. MuJoCo at 2 mm bends 37% less than the reference. After transfer, the error is 4% at the fitted pressure and 8% at half of it. - Cable actuators on all three backends: tendons through via points embedded in the elements, potential T L (implicit in the reference, explicit forces with a stability check on MuJoCo/SOFA), YAML/Python/ROS control. - Check: the cable-bent cantilever. The reference matches Euler–Bernoulli within 0.3% up to 0.27 rad, with the Neo-Hookean tangent under the cable's pre-compression. - Multi-material bodies (body.zones: elements with their own material, e.g. a strain-limiting layer): any law in the reference, per-zone force fields on SOFA, per-element material data on MuJoCo. Check: a two-material cable beam against composite Euler–Bernoulli (reference within 1.4% at small load). - PneuNet finger (pneunet shape: chambers, channel, conforming strain-limiting layer). MuJoCo and SOFA agree to 0.1% and bend 24% less than the reference at 8 kPa. A two-card transfer (body and layer) brings MuJoCo to 2.9%, holding at 11 kPa (3.2%) and on a 4-chamber finger (4.3%). - Bodies from files (mesh_file: STEP/IGES/BREP, STL/OBJ, .msh/VTK/Medit, .geo through gmsh). Physical groups become regions and zones, closed inner shells become cavity, and boxes name faces. Several CAD solids are bonded into one body. softsim export --cad writes the parametric shapes as STEP. The PneuNet read back from its own STEP is the same body (volumes exact) and bends within 0.5% on MuJoCo. - Zones with their own density on all backends. Check: a cantilever with a heavy outer half sags as Euler–Bernoulli says (reference within 0.15%). - Stroke-controlled cables (control: stroke: a servo reeling in a tendon of given stiffness, slack when short; implicit in the reference, explicit with a stability check on MuJoCo/SOFA). Check: the reference within 0.8% of Euler–Bernoulli with the beam's bending and axial compliance in series with the tendon. - Region forces (type: force: a dead load spread over a surface region by area, consistent on the reference's quadratic faces). Check: a tip-loaded cantilever converges to beam theory. - Moving mount (body.mount_path: the fixed regions follow a minimum-jerk translation), simulated in the mount's frame on every backend. Check: the reference agrees with a world-frame run with prescribed base motion to 0.03% (second order in the step). - Prescribed region motion (body.prescribed: any surface region follows a minimum-jerk path per axis, so a roller or a grip; the reaction force is an output on every backend). Check: a roller tension test. The reference gives the exact homogeneous stress (1e-7 at 10%, 1e-5 at 30% stretch), and force control with the reported reaction stretches the bar by the prescribed amount on all three backends; a fast pull checks the reaction against the body's momentum. - Rotating mount (body.mount_rotation: the fixed regions turn about an axis, minimum-jerk waypoints, composing with the translation). MuJoCo and SOFA simulate in the mount's frame with rotated gravity and the Euler, centrifugal and Coriolis forces; the reference runs in the world with the base nodes driven along the rotation (trapezoidal rule). Checks: the terms against numerical differentiation of a free particle, the applied forces against m a, the rotating rod's centrifugal stretch (reference +2.8%, MuJoCo -1.6%, SOFA -2.3%), the Euler lag at the start, and a spinning round beam that must move as a still one (reference 6.4%; the linear-tet backends 17-21%, from the mesh's anisotropy and implicit Euler, with each broken force 48-355%). - Cable anchor spread over a face (anchor: <region>: the end force becomes the linear traction with the same resultant and moment, on all backends). Check: the reference is within 0.5% of Euler-Bernoulli at the tip (a point anchor 2.6% low), and under stroke control within 0.7% with no stiff cap (a point anchor -19%). - Zones with their own damping (reference only: a Prony series, or none, per zone; MuJoCo and SOFA have one damping per body and refuse). Check: the plate force of a body with a quarter-section zone of another series is the area-weighted sum of each series' exact history. - Cable finger (cable_finger shape: segments cut by slots, a tendon through the web, path: geometry). Check: exact mesh volume, one segment is Euler-Bernoulli (-0.9%), four segments bend 2.54 times as far, mesh converged to 0.5%; a plane-section beam model (1.55 times) is a lower bound. - Analytic checks: the closed-end thick tube (Lame, free extension) on the reference converges at second order (radial -10% to -0.5% from 4 to 1.3 mm; axial strain +0.3% at 1.8 mm); SOFA's Rayleigh alpha against a free fall with linear drag (the implicit-Euler recurrence to 1e-12). - Closed-loop control from Python: Simulation.run(controller=...) (a PI loop holding a cable beam's tip angle is a test).

Still to do: - ~~More actuators: a constant-rate rotating mount~~ done 2026-11-11: waypoints [time, angle, rate] (actuation.md). - Backend mappings (optional, for speed or stability): tried and not shipped. SoftRobots' CableConstraint (plugin present in the SOFA v26.06 install; load it with RequiredPlugin SoftRobots, via points as a BarycentricMapping child, pullPoint a little behind the first point) in valueType="force" reproduces the explicit cable exactly: the cable cantilever's tip angle at 0.7 N (a step, 2 mm, 1 ms) agreed to 1e-14 at steps 50, 100, 200 and 500 (0.2837, 0.1523, 0.2471, 0.2861 rad). The solver's λ is an impulse, so the value must be force × dt (a force of 0.01 N without the factor gave 6 m/s). A force-type constraint is still an applied tension at the step's start, so it has no stability advantage over ConstantForceField; the one that would is the displacement type (a rigid tendon, stiffness → ∞), which is a different model from the finite-stiffness tendon here, and SOFA-only. Not pursued: it needs a rigid-tendon option in the config first. SurfacePressureConstraint was not tried. MuJoCo spatial tendons attach to sites on bodies, not to barycentric points inside flex elements, so the cable's via points would have to be vertices.

docs.title: M7: pneumatic finger (in progress; blocked on a data decision)
docs.text:
PneuNet scenario (pressure → bending angle, tip force, cavity volume), public datasets registered with DOI and licence, and a generic experiment API so calibration and plots work for any scenario. Yeoh in SOFA (custom force field) or refused.

Done: - PneuNet scenario, backends compared and MuJoCo transferred (above). - Generic experiment API: softsim fit (any observable column of any scenario against a registered measured table, curve or series; docs/experiments.md). Checked by a twin experiment: it recovers a hidden modulus to 0.4% (clean) and 3.5% (1% noise); four code mutants are caught. - Yeoh in SOFA: refused, with the softsim material project hint. - Finer meshes on the GPU: the element kernels run in chunks (a 100k-element launch asked the 12 GB card for 4.8 GB and failed); the reference PneuNet now runs to 0.7 mm (152k tetrahedra, 25 min for four loads) and converges to within about 0.4% per step; the 1.5 mm reference is 3.6% under-bent (docs/actuation.md).

Open: real data. No public pressure–angle dataset with a geometry and material I can read was usable; the options and my recommendation are in decisions.md, entry 3.

docs.title: M8: cable finger, soft arm and rods
docs.text: Done on the reference: the cable-finger shape and scenario (cable_finger, docs/actuation.md) and a two-segment cable arm with stiff disks (cable_arm.yaml, within 2% of piecewise Euler–Bernoulli). Not done: a rod (Cosserat) backend for slender bodies (SOFA BeamAdapter, PyElastica or our own): chosen by the recommendation, SOFA BeamAdapter (decisions.md, entry 4). Done: --backend rod (backends/rod.md): a slender clamped body of any scenario is reduced to beam frames (section stiffnesses from the tets with material zones exact; the mesh follows the frames), cables and region forces carried by virtual work. Verified on the tip load (0.8641 mm vs E–B 0.864), cable cantilever, 64° large rotation (arc of the compressed beam), layered section and the S of the two-segment arm (linear E–B within 0.7%; the 3D reference is 8% lower from the compression stiffening 1 + 2N/EA, which a materially linear rod cannot have); 16 tests, 6 mutants caught, a figure. Open: alpha damping is inert on BeamAdapter's mass (refused), the explicit cable step limit (the rod backend's; the SOFA FEM cable is now implicit), and rods that are not columns along z (curved or branched), PneuNet-like bodies being out of scope.

docs.title: M9: soft gripper and grasping
docs.text:
N-finger gripper on a rigid palm. Grasp metrics (success, contact patch, forces, slip, pull-out). Contact quality work, including the M4 SOFA artefacts, finger self-collision (done for MuJoCo and SOFA, one geometry) and a friction benchmark. A grasp benchmark grid.

Started 2026-11-06: two-finger gripper on the reference, a fast finger fitted to it, a local live page and a grasp map (gripper.md). Two finite-element grasps with Coulomb friction (10 g held, 30 g dropped) agree with the fast finger and play in the page's Truth tab. The finite-element finger's tip force is about 5.5 times below the measurement with its tip sliding on the gauge, and about twice above with its tip stuck to it: the unrecorded contact explains the gap, so the force cannot test the model (2026-11-11, actuation.md).

2026-11-11: friction benchmark (scenarios/actuation/sliding_block.yaml, benchmarks/sliding_block.yaml and sticking_block.yaml, tests/test_friction.py). A silicone block pushed across the ground against exact Coulomb sliding: all three backends within 0.8-0.94%. Below the limit, MuJoCo creeps at 0.13 mm/s (soft constraints) and the reference at a rate set by its time step (its friction smoothing is per step; decisions.md, entry 6).

2026-11-11: self-collision (body.self_collision, tests/test_self_collision.py). A finger pulled until its slot closes: with self-collision on, the slot's walls stay apart (MuJoCo +0.19 mm, SOFA +0.10 mm); off, they pass through by 1.3 mm. fem and rod refuse it. Verified on one geometry only (actuation.md).

docs.title: M10: magnetic soft robots (MRE)
docs.text:
Soft-magnetic elastomer first, because that is what isotropic MRE fingers are: carbonyl-iron particles with no remanence, magnetised by the applied field. The energy is linear-magnetic with axes that follow the deformation, in a given field (uniform plus a point dipole); the field is not solved for. Then a permanent magnet's field, an MRE finger against a measured force, and a magnetic gripper. A hard-magnetic model (fixed magnetisation) follows if a design needs it.

Started 2026-11-08: softsim/fem/magnetic.py on the reference, checked against a turned body's energy, the pull up a dipole's gradient and a cantilever's closed form up to buckling (tests/test_magnetic.py).

2026-11-09 (magnetic.md):

  • Config. magneto_active cards take a susceptibility or an iron fraction, with block demagnetising factors. A scene-level magnetic_field: holds a uniform field and ring or disc magnets, which can move along paths and can be solid.
  • Field. The magnets' fields are exact, checked against current loops to 1e-7.
  • Checks. A bar built from the config follows its closed form to 2.2%. A mutation sweep tries 32 slips.
  • Against Bernat et al.'s gripper (arXiv:2407.13477), digitised from the paper's vector figures:
  • The rolling torque is flat, as in their ANSYS. The point where it falls to zero suggests a strip about 2 mm thick.
  • With the susceptibility from the recipe alone, the torque is 58-66% of theirs.
  • The 0.7 N finger force is not checked yet: the paper does not give the contact point.
  • Solid magnets. A magnet can also be a rigid cylinder for contact. Each magnet has a chamfer (edge, 0.2 mm) that softens its field's singular rims and rounds its contact surface: the singular rims had drawn a strip into the magnet's corner.
  • Fixed: H inside a magnet. It is now B / mu0 - M; taking B / mu0 made a false well under the rim.
  • Finger force.
  • Energy balance for a free end peeled along the rim's tangent gives 0.24-0.28 N on our torque and 0.44 N on ANSYS's, against 0.66-0.83 N measured.
  • A clamped strip pulled that way cannot peel. Finite elements show the force rising past 1.9 N.
  • So the measured force depends on the gauge's unrecorded contact point.
  • Not yet simulated:
  • the 15 mm strip, whose overhanging flaps snap onto the magnet's poles;
  • the strip closing from a gap: it hits the magnet at metres per second.
  • Next:
  • ~~saturation~~ done 2026-11-11: a tanh law from the card's saturation_magnetization (0 keeps the linear law), checked against the closed forms (magnetic.md);
  • the finger against a gauge, once the set-up is known;
  • ~~a hard-magnetic model~~ done 2026-11-11: remanent magnetisation -mu0 (F M_r) . H (Zhao et al. 2019), checked against closed forms (magnetic.md).
  • ~~magnetic zones~~ done 2026-11-11: zones carry their own magneto_active card (hard, soft or none), the energy assembled per element; two zones of opposite remanence cancel and a non-magnetic one halves the energy, to 1e-12; a zone with induced magnetisation needs explicit demagnetising factors (block is refused);
  • ~~a hard-magnetic gripper on the reference~~ done 2026-11-11: a U-shaped body with two oppositely magnetised arms closes in a uniform field (scenarios/magnetic/hard_magnetic_gripper.yaml); the arm's bending is the cantilever's under a distributed couple to 1.4% at 1 mm (0.5% at 0.75 mm), the tip 17-18% more because the palm rotates at the root. Not yet: gripping an object (a GPU-machine job, magnetic.md).

docs.title: M11: design and control toolkit
docs.text:
Quasi-static inverse control (done: softsim inverse by repeated equilibrium solves, and the SoftRobots.Inverse fast path on SOFA, --method sofa-qp; see control.md), reduced-order surrogates for real-time ROS 2 control (done: quasi-static polynomial/RBF maps and a linear DMD model, softsim surrogate; closed-loop Controller with surrogate feedforward, integral feedback and an MPC-lite option, surrogate.md; Koopman not done), design optimisation over parametric geometry (softsim optimize), and sim-to-real identification from short recorded motions.

  • Design optimisation (done): softsim optimize <job.yaml> (design.md). Nelder-Mead over dotted design parameters (units, bounds, log, integer, tied keys), objective maximise/minimise/target on any summary metric (or a ratio), constraints as penalties with the best chosen among feasible evaluations and infeasibility reported, resumable evaluation log, parallel initial simplex. Checked on the cable cantilever against a known maximum (the bound) and a bisection reference; the MuJoCo-locking bias of the optimum and the fem check are documented. Open in M11: sim-to-real identification.
  • SOFA fast path for inverse control (done): softsim/control/sofa_inverse.py, softsim inverse --method sofa-qp (control.md). The SoftRobots.Inverse plugin loads and works in the v26.06 binary (QPInverseProblemSolver, CableActuator, PositionEffector). The scene is built beside the SOFA backend, not inside it (no backend change). Cantilever tension within 0.6-1.2% of the repeated solve on the same backend and 7-11 times faster (1 s); the two-cable arm in 2.8 s where the repeated solve on SOFA does not settle (336 s, stalled, with the then explicit cable force; see the next bullet); a target beyond the bounds gives the bounded solution, flagged. The cable bounds go in as force * dt and the tension is read as lambda / dt (the M6 note on impulses). Pressure actuators (SurfacePressureActuator on the cavity surface) are in: the bounds go in as pressure * dt like the cables, the cavity triangles need the opposite winding, and the effector weight 1e6 fixes a badly scaled QP; the bending tube recovers 4 kPa to 0.03% (7 times faster than the repeated solve on SOFA) and the PneuNet 5 kPa to 0.05%. Also in: angle targets with any actuator (the effector goal is moved along a free axis by a Broyden iteration on the goals; the bending tube's tilt recovers 4 kPa to 0.0005%), a pressure and a cable together (scenarios/inflation/bending_cable.yaml, tip x and z recover 3983 Pa / 0.19992 N for 4000 Pa / 0.2 N; angle plus position 0.11% / 0.01%) and stroke-controlled cables (solved as tensions, stroke read back, stroke bounds iterated: 1.4997 mm for 1.5 mm, 1.0002 mm at a 1 mm limit). Open: a true orientation effector (this build has no Rigid3d one: PositionEffector, CableEffector, VolumeEffector, BarycentricCenterEffector), output constraints, anchored cables and force actuators, several bodies.
  • The SOFA cable's limit cycle (done): the explicit follower force swung the two-cable arm at every step from 10 ms to 0.25 ms (the swing grows as the step shrinks, so it is not the lag), it vanishes with a linear or corotational elastic law and with the force-type CableConstraint it does not (identical to the explicit run). The cable's stabilising lateral stiffness was missing from the implicit system while the hyperelastic law's geometric stiffness, which it balances, was in it (inferred from these runs). The backend now builds tension-controlled cables as springs with per-step rest lengths (SofaBackend._add_cable): the arm settles at 5 ms to 1 ms (tip x 4.0025 mm, z 118.514 mm) and the repeated solve converges (control.md). Stroke-controlled and anchored cables are still explicit.
  • Surrogates (done): softsim surrogate <job.yaml> (surrogate.md). Seeded Latin-hypercube samples settled with the inverse solver's equilibrium code, a polynomial (degree by cross-validation) or RBF fit, held-out validation, a resumable sample log keyed on the scenario and code hash, JSON evaluable from numpy. softsim inverse --method surrogate solves in 26-38 ms, with an optional verifying simulation. MuJoCo: cantilever held-out error 2e-7 rad; arm 21 um (tip x), the known 0.45 / 0.15 N found to 0.01% (the repeated solve: 0.4%) 1500 times faster once fitted (the samples cost 3-4 repeated solves). Optional DMD-with-control dynamic model, held-out rollout error 0.4-1.1% of the travel on the cantilever. Open: Koopman (nonlinear) dynamics, closed-loop use in a ROS 2 node, surrogates on SOFA or the reference.

docs.title: M12: GPU backend and learning (GPU machine)
docs.text:
Evaluate MuJoCo Warp/MJX, NVIDIA Warp FEM and Genesis for correctness, speed and differentiability, and implement the best behind the same interface with a batched API. Gymnasium environments per robot, with domain randomisation over the calibrated error bars. Run the deferred long calibrations (bulk-modulus refit, finer meshes).

CPU groundwork done: Gymnasium environments on the MuJoCo CPU backend (softsim.envs, extra rl): a generic reach-task env from YAML, two registered examples (cable beam, two-cable arm), domain randomisation over the card's uncertainty and config ranges, SyncVectorEnv compatible; see envs.md. Open: the batched GPU backend. Also done: a PneuNet bending env (softsim/PneuNetBend-v0, coarse thick-walled variant, 7 steps/s), a reduced-gripper grasp-and-lift env (softsim/ReducedGripperLift-v0, 150 steps/s, randomised mass and friction) and tools/train_baseline.py, a numpy CEM baseline with measured gains over random actions (envs.md). Open: the same for the FE gripper, deep-RL baselines (stable-baselines3) as an optional extra.

docs.title: M13: benchmarks, docs, release (release-ready; waiting for the tag)
docs.text:
Done: softsim bench writes docs/benchmarks.md (every validated scenario × every backend: error vs data, wall time, mesh); a docs site with tutorials; contribution guides for robots, presets and datasets; CI (lint, tests on Python 3.10 and 3.12, a core-only job, the docs build, and a weekly SOFA job); a release workflow (sdist and wheel, PyPI trusted publishing, docs deploy on a v* tag); and packaged example configs (softsim examples copy DIR) so a pip install can run the drop test, the cable and PneuNet scenarios and the Gymnasium environments. The wheel and sdist pass twine check and install and run in clean environments.

Open (needs the maintainer): set up the PyPI trusted publisher (project softsim, workflow release.yml, environment pypi), enable GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch, set the 0.1.0 date in CHANGELOG.md and CITATION.cff, and push the tag v0.1.0.

docs.title: Open items
docs.text:
• The 500 g first contact stops 2–3× harder and faster than any model allows, and the tracking is confirmed independently. It lands about 11° tilted in the image plane, with an unknown out-of-plane tilt. The cause is unknown, and it is kept out of fits until understood (M5).
  • Rate-dependent tack: the cohesive law is elastic. The 50 g weight's peel-and-flip loses more energy than an elastic bond would.
  • Spring mounts on SOFA need per-contact force reporting (SOFA reports contacts by momentum balance, which can't separate support–ground from support–specimen).
  • The bulk-modulus refit (calibrations/ecoflex_00_10_drop_sofa_ogden_bulk.yaml) was stopped after 12 evaluations without improvement; it targets 500 g, whose data is now in question. Its evaluations are kept and it resumes if re-run.
  • Rate dependence: Prony now runs on every backend (M5). What is missing is rate data for silicones, and a test of whether any Prony spectrum explains the heavy impacts.

  • (Done, 2026-11-12: the SOFA frictionless-plate artefact was friction, and the rim-flare ground penetration an alarm distance shorter than the per-step travel; backends/sofa.md.)

  • SOFA under the tilted 500 g impact (2026-11-12): with the measured 11° landing tilt the SOFA fits blow up at 5 mm / 0.05 ms; try a finer step or mesh (GPU machine), or refit with the tilt. The fits made before the tilt existed are re-simulated without it (tilt: false, experiments.md).

docs.title: Later
docs.text: Material-characterisation scenarios (quasi-static compression, indentation, bending), more robot morphologies (crawlers, swimmers, continuum arms), and fluid–structure coupling.

docs.title: ROS 2 integration (Humble)
docs.text:
Three packages under ros2/ wrap the core library. The physics stays in softsim, so anything the CLI can run, the node can run.

Package Type Contents softsim_interfaces ament_cmake SoftBodyState, ContactWrench(Array), ScenarioMetrics, SimulationStatus; SetMaterial, RunAction services softsim_ros ament_python softsim_node: generic node that runs any scenario softsim_bringup ament_cmake softsim.launch.py, RViz config, and the repository's scenarios/ installed to share/softsim_bringup/scenarios

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
softsim and MuJoCo live in the project venv (see the README), so build and run with the venv active. The node's shebang is /usr/bin/env python3, so it uses whichever Python is active.

source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m colcon build --base-paths ros2        # from the repository root
source install/setup.bash

Always run with the same venv active: the generated message modules are compiled against the venv's NumPy (1.26).

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
ros2 launch softsim_bringup softsim.launch.py                                   # drop test (20 g) + RViz
ros2 launch softsim_bringup softsim.launch.py config:=drop_test/cases/w100.yaml viewer:=true
ros2 launch softsim_bringup softsim.launch.py on_finish:=loop                   # repeat the scenario forever
ros2 launch softsim_bringup softsim.launch.py overrides:="drop.height=0.2;drop.tilt=[5 deg, 0]"
ros2 launch softsim_bringup softsim.launch.py headless:=true output_dir:=runs/ros   # batch: run, save, exit
Launch argument Default Meaning scenario drop_test default config is <scenario>/scenario.yaml config scenario YAML, absolute or relative to the installed scenarios/ overrides ;-separated key=value (same syntax as softsim --set) rviz true start RViz with rviz/softsim.rviz viewer false MuJoCo passive viewer headless false no GUI; run once, save to output_dir (default runs/ros), shut down output_dir save results when a run finishes on_finish hold hold, loop or stop publish_every 1 publish every N output samples

The node (softsim) also takes backend, frame_id, publish_soft_state, metric_topics, autostart and scenarios_dir as parameters; see the docstring in softsim_ros/node.py.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
All of these are under the node namespace (/softsim/...), except /clock and /tf.

Topic Type Notes /clock rosgraph_msgs/Clock simulated time, monotonic across resets /tf world → each rigid body frame rigid/<name>/pose, rigid/<name>/twist PoseStamped, TwistStamped world frame rigid_markers MarkerArray (latched) primitive parts, frame-locked to TF soft/<name>/points PointCloud2 soft-body vertices, world frame soft_markers MarkerArray soft-body surface meshes (TRIANGLE_LIST) soft/<name>/state SoftBodyState only with publish_soft_state:=true contacts ContactWrenchArray per body pair: force by body_a on body_b, centre of pressure ground_reaction WrenchStamped total ground wrench, torque about the world origin metrics ScenarioMetrics all scenario metrics; for the drop test: indentation, compression, bulge, forces, ... metrics/<name> std_msgs/Float64 one topic per metric (rqt_plot / PlotJuggler) status SimulationStatus 2 Hz: sim time, real-time factor, paused/finished, warnings actuators/<name>/state std_msgs/Float64 the actuator's value in effect: pressure [Pa], cable tension [N], a stroke-controlled cable's stroke [m], or a region force [N] actuators/<name>/command (subscribed) std_msgs/Float64 hold this value from the next step on; NaN returns to the schedule; a negative tension is ignored with a warning (a negative stroke pays the cable out)

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service Type Example reset std_srvs/Trigger set_paused std_srvs/SetBool {data: true} save std_srvs/Trigger write the run so far to output_dir (or runs/) set_material softsim_interfaces/SetMaterial {body: specimen, material: '{preset: ecoflex_00_10, elastic: {youngs_modulus: 40 kPa}}'}, or change single values of the current material: {body: specimen, material: '', overrides: ['elastic.youngs_modulus=40 kPa']} action softsim_interfaces/RunAction {action: drop, arguments: '{preset: czopek2026_w050, height: 0.2}'}
